en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
17. The Mansion of Kesakārī “This mansion is beautiful and radiant,
with pillars of beryl, eternally well-constructed;”
This place of mine, born from the ripening of my karma, is completely covered on all sides by golden trees.
These former stingy ones have been reborn there.
By your own karma, you have come here as one of a hundred thousand; illustrious one,
you stand illuminating us, a deity from a former life.
Just as the moon shines forth, having surpassed the host of stars like the king of constellations,
even so do you [shine] over this assembly of celestial nymphs.
Shining with glory, you resplendently manifest.
From where have you come, O Anomadassinī,
to be reborn here in this palace of mine?
“Even as the gods of the Thirty-three with Indra at their head,
we all do not tire of beholding you.
“O Sakka, as for that which you ask me— ”
“From where have you passed away to come here?
“There is a city named Bārāṇasī in Kāsī;
there, in the past, I was a hairdresser.”
With minds full of serene confidence in the Buddha and the Dhamma,
having reached a state of certainty and freedom from doubt regarding the Saṅgha,
those whose precepts are unbroken have attained the fruit.
“Fixed in the Dhamma of full enlightenment, you are free from all affliction. “We rejoice in that; welcome to you!
You shine with the glory of the Dhamma.”
With a mind full of serene confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma,
and the Saṅgha that has reached certainty and is free from doubt;
with the precepts unbroken and the fruit attained—
“In the fixed, flawless Dhamma of full enlightenment.
Thus ends the seventeenth *Kesakārī-vimāna*.
Its summary verse:
Five seats, three boats,
two lamps, sesame, and alms-food;
two husbands, two daughters-in-law, and the North.
"Sirimā Kesakārikā":
thus is the chapter named.
This is the first chapter in the *Itthivimāna*.
